{"m": "gpt-4o-mini", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
My younger brother broke our grandmother's antique vase while playing ball inside. When our parents came home furious, I said I did it. I was grounded for a month. He never confessed, and I never told. He was only seven and would have been devastated.

CANDIDATE A:
My younger brother crashed my car and let me take the blame from our parents. A week later, overwhelmed with guilt, he confessed everything. He paid for the repairs himself and accepted the grounding he'd originally avoided.

CANDIDATE B:
My coworker accidentally deleted a critical database backup the night before an audit. When our CTO demanded to know who was responsible, I claimed it was my mistake. I took the formal warning on my record. She was six months pregnant and couldn't afford to lose her job.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:7"}
content: {"choice": "B", "reason": "Both stories involve a person taking the blame for another's mistake to protect them from negative consequences, resulting in personal sacrifice."}
